paper.title: ArcMemo: Abstract Reasoning Composition with Lifelong LLM Memory
paper.central_claim: Concept-level (abstract, modular, natural-language) memory distilled from solution traces and selectively retrieved into the prompt enables test-time continual learning without weight updates; on ARC-AGI-1 it gives a 7.5% relative gain over a strong no-memory baseline (55.17 to 59.33), is the only memory design above baseline at all tested inference scales, and dynamically updating memory at test time outperforms fixed settings.

provenance.notes: actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref are not exposed to the worker inside this dispatch; model_type is the claude-kimi type overlay assigned by the controller (agent_model=haiku -> claude-sonnet-5-5[1m]).

evidence.quote: Although effective for closely related problems, they have diminished utility for problems superficially different from prior experiences.
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap: instance-level reasoning memories transfer poorly to superficially different problems.

evidence.quote: the lack of structure and modularity makes scaling with more experiences challenging.
evidence.support_explanation: Author critique of the monolithic evolving-summary neighbour (Dynamic Cheatsheet).

evidence.quote: For future queries, relevant concepts are selectively retrieved and integrated into the prompt, enabling test-time continual learning without weight updates.
evidence.support_explanation: Central design: abstract concept memory, selective retrieval, prompt injection, no weight update.

evidence.quote: Moreover, dynamically updating memory during test-time outperforms fixed settings, supporting the hypothesis that accumulating and abstracting patterns enables further solutions in a form of self-improvement.
evidence.support_explanation: Author claim that test-time memory updating (the self-improvement part) beats fixed memory.

evidence.quote: The main requirement for our memory system is that some feedback is available at test-time (e.g. via test cases or self-reflection).
evidence.support_explanation: Retention relies on an external correctness signal; its exact source in continual updates is not specified.

evidence.quote: Incorrect traces still likely contain vital signal, but error identification/credit assignment remains an open challenge that we leave to future efforts.
evidence.support_explanation: Only correct traces feed memory; no contrast with failures, no credit assignment.

evidence.quote: The organization of memory entries on a collective level is another design surface we leave for future exploration; we use a flat collection of entries for simplicity.
evidence.support_explanation: Flat additive store; organization deferred.

evidence.quote: This minimal formulation does not consider the existing contents of memory while adding new entries for simplicity and scaling reasons.
evidence.support_explanation: OE write ignores existing entries (no dedup/merge/update); consolidation deferred to selection and solving.

evidence.quote: We encourage the model to reuse and revise existing concepts by updating concept descriptions, parameter lists, relevance cues, and implementation notes.
evidence.support_explanation: PS write can revise existing concepts using a compressed view of memory (partial maintenance), no deletion/forgetting stated.

evidence.quote: PS Selection instructs a reasoning model to systematically explore the problem
evidence.support_explanation: Read path for PS: reasoning-model exploration with relevance cues and type annotations.

evidence.quote: manually authored Python solutions for 160 puzzles from the public train split to act as “seeds” to recombine into their synthetic dataset.
evidence.support_explanation: Seed solutions are human-written, from the train split (external source, not agent experience).

evidence.quote: We reuse these solutions to seed our memory rather than training data.
evidence.support_explanation: Main memory is seeded from the 160 external solutions.

evidence.quote: we evaluate a randomly selected 100-puzzle subset of the public val split.
evidence.support_explanation: Evaluation set: 100 random public-validation puzzles; separate split from the seeds.

evidence.quote: our method improves the official score from 55.17 to 59.33 (+7.5% relative gain over a strong no-memory baseline)
evidence.support_explanation: Headline result at standard compute (2 parallel attempts, 0 retries).

evidence.quote: ArcMemo-PS is the only setting that outperforms the baseline consistently at every tested scale.
evidence.support_explanation: Per-scale table; the claim is directionally true in all 9 cells but with small margins (retry1/2: +0.17 to +2.5).

No-memory o4-mini baseline official score 55.17 with SD 3.18 over 3 runs; ArcMemo-PS 59.33 (0.29). The +4.16 gain is about 1.3 baseline SDs; at retry1/retry2 gains over baseline (0.17 to 2.5) are below one baseline SD (2.84 to 3.33).
ArcMemo-PS official score 59.33, SD 0.29 over 3 runs (note much smaller SD than the baseline).

evidence.quote: However, there still exist certain scale regimes where the no-selection setting has a better score.
evidence.support_explanation: Selection ablation (Table 2): selection helps in 7/9 cells, mostly at retry 0 (55.17 vs 59.33 official, equal to the no-memory baseline); reversed at retry1/2 k=3 (73.0 vs 72.5; 76.0 vs 75.5).
PS without selection at retry0 k=1: 46.83 (SD 5.25) vs 49.33 with selection; at official k=2: 55.17 vs 59.33, i.e. no gain over the no-memory baseline without selection.

evidence.quote: continually updating memory with new self-generated solutions leads to improved puzzle-solving performance.
evidence.support_explanation: Author claim on continual updates; only the OE format is tested, every 10 problems.

evidence.quote: In particular, we find that the performance improvement emerges at later iterations in sequential inference scaling.
evidence.support_explanation: Gain only at high retry depth.

Table 3 (continual minus fixed, OE): retry0 k1/k2/k3 = -1.67/-0.67/0; retry1 = +0.50/-0.67/-3.00; retry2 = +1.67/+2.33/+1.00. Positive in 4 of 9 cells, negative in 4, zero in 1; cells such as 65.00 (0.00) and 56.00 (0.00) report SD 0.00 without explanation. PS is not tested with continual updates.

evidence.quote: However, continual updates also introduce dependencies on evaluation order.
evidence.support_explanation: Authors acknowledge order/batch dependence of the continual-update claim.

evidence.quote: In other experiments, we used fixed memory to prioritize throughput and avoid the potentially confounding effect of order dependencies.
evidence.support_explanation: All main results use fixed (frozen) memory.

evidence.locator: App C Token Efficiency; material line 1680
evidence.quote: We observe that memory-augmented runs tend to increase output token usage.
evidence.support_explanation: Memory runs emit more output tokens; a matched-exploration-budget control is absent.

evidence.quote: to the tokens used by the reasoning model for strictly puzzle solving.
evidence.support_explanation: Token-efficiency plot counts only solver reasoning tokens, not abstraction (GPT-4.1) or selection calls.

evidence.locator: App C Embedding-based Retrieval; material line 1700
evidence.quote: proved ineffective, lowering the score from 0.26 to 0.22, marking a 15% reduction.
evidence.support_explanation: Motivates reasoning-based selection: embedding retrieval over abstract entries hurt (o3-mini backbone, early test).

evidence.locator: App C Concept Specificity; material line 1690
evidence.quote: higher levels of specificity correspond to better solve rates.
evidence.support_explanation: n=10 pilot: more specific concepts solve more, in tension with the abstraction premise (authors attribute it to retrieval trade-off).

evidence.quote: the substantial sampling variance we observed
evidence.support_explanation: Authors report large run-to-run sampling variance on the 100-puzzle subset.

evidence.quote: We manually analyzed these puzzles and found that only 40% of new solves in the cheatsheet setting were related to memory elements actually in the generated cheatsheet.
evidence.support_explanation: Manual attribution of 10 differing puzzles; blinding not stated.

evidence.quote: In contrast, 100% of new solves from ArcMemo-PS (-selection) can be linked to concept memory contents.
evidence.support_explanation: Suggestive attribution evidence, small n.

evidence.quote: DC-Cu (labeled “cheatsheet”) that uses a frozen memory to match other settings.
evidence.support_explanation: Cheatsheet baseline is a frozen re-implementation; whether it is seeded with the same 160 solutions is not stated.

evidence.quote: While the official evaluation scheme allows different test cases solved by different attempts to be ensembled,
evidence.support_explanation: A strict scoring regime (one program must solve all test cases) is also reported.

evidence.quote: Dynamic Cheatsheet maintains a unified buffer that is adapted continuously.
evidence.support_explanation: Nearest neighbour description; full text of DC/BoT/MemP is not in the pinned materials.

evidence.quote: MemP in particular is a concurrent work that also demonstrates the efficacy of abstraction
evidence.support_explanation: Concurrent abstraction-memory neighbour (action-sequence rewriting in agentic settings).

evidence.quote: ARC-AGI-2 was released mid-project as a harder successor benchmark
evidence.support_explanation: Single benchmark generation (ARC-AGI-1); ARC-AGI-2 not run.

signatures.object: Flat external memory of concept entries (OE: situation/suggestion pairs; PS: parameterized typed types/structures/routines with relevance cues and implementation notes) injected into an o4-mini program-synthesis solver prompt; baselines: no memory, frozen Dynamic-Cheatsheet-style summary.
signatures.information: Verified solution traces (post-hoc derivation / pseudocode) of seed puzzles and, in the continual variant, self-generated solutions; a correctness feedback signal is assumed available; labels may be absent at inference; evaluation puzzles are separate from the 160 train-split seeds.
signatures.operation: Write: GPT-4.1 abstracts a solution into OE or PS entries (PS revises existing entries using a compressed view of memory). Read: OE = VLM caption of the puzzle + LLM top-k match against situation fields; PS = reasoning-model exploration guided by relevance cues and type annotations.
signatures.output: Subset of concept entries injected into the solver prompt.
signatures.conditions: Trace-level correctness feedback required; abstract entries break embedding retrieval, hence reasoning-based selection.
signatures.feedback: Execution of the synthesized program against reference pairs (retries) and test cases.
signatures.selection_rule: No measured admission or marginal-utility test; entries come from (assumed) verified-correct solutions; read-time top-k / reasoning-based selection only.
signatures.persistence: Additive flat store; OE write ignores existing contents; PS can revise; no deletion, forgetting, versioning, rollback or conflict handling (deferred to future work).
signatures.later_use: Retrieved for each new puzzle in later passes.
signatures.claimed_effect: Official score 55.17 -> 59.33 at 0 retries (ARC-AGI-1, 100 validation puzzles, o4-mini, mean of 3 runs); only memory design above baseline in all 9 inference-scale cells.
signatures.failure_boundary: Needs feedback; retrieval-specificity tension; flat store; single benchmark; gains concentrate at low inference compute.

retention_trace.proposed_change: new/revised concept entries abstracted from verified solution traces
retention_trace.selection_data_rule: assumed-correct traces only; no marginal-effect test
retention_trace.measured_gain: +4.16 official points at retry0, +0.17..+2.5 at other scales (within ~1 baseline SD)

signatures.object: OE concept memory updated during evaluation (every 10 problems) with newly self-generated solutions.
signatures.information: Solver outputs on the evaluation stream; which feedback certifies a solution before it is written (reference pairs vs hidden test outputs) is not stated.
signatures.operation: Re-run the OE write operation on new solutions every k=10 problems, then read as in S1.
signatures.output: Grown OE memory used by later problems/passes.
signatures.conditions: Order and batching dependence acknowledged; fixed memory used elsewhere to avoid confounding.
signatures.feedback: Self-generated solutions verified by tests (source unspecified).
signatures.later_use: Subsequent problems and subsequent retry passes over the test set.
signatures.claimed_effect: Improvement emerges at higher retry depth (OE only).
signatures.failure_boundary: Evaluation stream equals update stream; PS not tested; mixed cells (better than fixed in 4/9).

gap.author_gap: Reasoning insights are discarded when the context resets; existing reasoning memories are instance-level (coupled to the source problem) or monolithic summaries, which transfer poorly and scale badly without selection.
gap.checked_gap: Partly confirmed. The changed object (entry abstraction level + read-time selection) is specific and neighbours are named, but no experiment shows instance-level memories failing on ARC while abstract ones succeed, and the authors own n=10 pilot finds more specific concepts solve more.

gap.residue: Retrieval over abstract entries is hard (embedding retrieval hurt); consolidation/hierarchy and order-robust updates left to future work.
gap.stakes: Without abstraction and selection a growing reasoning memory either overflows context or distracts the solver.
gap.method_response: Concept formats (OE/PS) written by abstraction prompts, reasoning-based selection, optional continual updates.

claims.text: ArcMemo-PS improves the official ARC-AGI-1 score over a no-memory o4-mini baseline (59.33 vs 55.17) and is above baseline at all tested inference scales.
claims.setting: o4-mini (medium), 100 random public-validation puzzles, program-synthesis evaluation with execution feedback, fixed memory seeded from 160 hand-written train-split solutions
claims.baseline_control: same model, same retries and parallel attempts, no memory; plus frozen cheatsheet and OE variants
claims.selection_vs_test: seeds from train split, evaluation on validation split (separate)
claims.result_denominator: 100 puzzles x 3 runs; official oracle@2 59.33 (SD 0.29) vs 55.17 (SD 3.18); retry1 67.33 vs 66.67; retry2 70.83 vs 69.00
claims.allowed_conclusion: A small positive effect (about 1.3 baseline SD at retry0, below 1 SD elsewhere) on a 100-puzzle subset; not shown to be independent of extra exploration.

claims.text: Reasoning-based concept selection improves performance and token cost.
claims.setting: PS with vs without selection, same seeds
claims.result_denominator: better with selection in 7/9 cells; retry0 k=2 59.33 vs 55.17; reversed at retry1/2 k=3
claims.allowed_conclusion: Selection supplies the whole gain at the official standard-compute setting and little at higher retry depth.

claims.text: Dynamically updating memory at test time outperforms fixed memory (self-improvement).
claims.setting: OE only, update every 10 problems with self-generated solutions
claims.selection_vs_test: update stream equals evaluation stream; order dependent
claims.result_denominator: continual better in 4/9 cells (retry2 all three, retry1 k1), worse in 4/9, equal in 1
claims.allowed_conclusion: At most a retry-depth-dependent gain for OE, not established for PS; abstract claim of outperforming fixed settings is overstated.

claims.text: Abstract, modular concepts are the most consistent memory design (vs instance-level or summary memory).
claims.setting: PS and OE vs frozen cheatsheet vs no memory
claims.result_denominator: PS above baseline in 9/9 cells, cheatsheet 6/9, OE 3/9
claims.allowed_conclusion: PS is the only variant above no-memory everywhere; the abstraction-vs-instance claim itself is untested.

claims.text: New solves under ArcMemo are more attributable to memory content (100%) than under the cheatsheet (40%).
claims.setting: manual inspection of 10 puzzles that differ between two systems
claims.allowed_conclusion: Suggestive only; authors themselves caveat causal reading.

assessment.level_note: Fixed memory seeded from external solutions improves held-out validation puzzles against a store-off control (small effect); the self-generated continual-update loop (the improver-style claim) is only task-level/mixed.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: An LLM-abstracted, selectively retrieved concept memory seeded from 160 external solutions gives a small, noisy gain (about +4 points official score at 0 retries, at most +2.5 at higher scales, about one baseline SD or less) on a 100-puzzle ARC-AGI-1 validation subset with o4-mini; the gain at standard compute depends on the selection step; self-generated continual updates help only at the highest retry depth for the OE format and PS is not tested.
assessment.not_supported: That abstraction beats instance-level memory; that test-time updating outperforms fixed memory in general; that gains are independent of extra exploration tokens.
unresolved: Which feedback certifies traces written during continual updates
Whether the cheatsheet baseline is seeded identically

G.reason: Specific, sourced gap (instance-coupled memories transfer poorly; monolithic summaries lack structure) with the changed object identified (entry abstraction level + selection) and named neighbours. But no experiment shows instance-level memory failing on ARC, the authors own specificity pilot points the other way, and neighbour full texts are not pinned.

M.reason: Mechanism is reconstructable (OE situation/suggestion vs PS typed parameterized concepts, post-hoc derivation/pseudocode before abstraction, reasoning-based selection motivated by observed failure of embedding retrieval). Distinguishing predictions are partly tested (selection necessity); the central hypothesis (abstraction beats instance-level) has no direct control and the write-time correctness gate is assumed.

X.reason: Write/read prompts and steps are described, but retention conditions are thin: flat additive store, OE write ignores existing contents, no admission test beyond assumed-correct traces, no forgetting/versioning/rollback/conflict handling (deferred), certifying signal for continual updates unspecified, order dependence acknowledged.

E.measurement.reason: Official ARC scoring on executed programs (oracle@2) plus strict single-program scoring in Table 5 is a credible verifier; 100 puzzles randomly chosen. Public-ARC exposure of the solver is not addressed (scored under holdout).

E.causality.reason: Store-off baseline with equal retries/parallel samples, selection ablation, cheatsheet and OE comparisons exist. Missing: instance-level memory under the same pipeline, matched-token control (memory runs emit more output tokens), and the continual-update comparison is mixed (better in 4 of 9 cells); attribution analysis is a manual 10-puzzle check.

E.holdout.reason: Fixed-memory runs seed from train split and test on validation puzzles (clean), but there is no public-ARC exposure audit, the lifelong/self-improvement claim is tested on the same stream whose order matters, the certifying feedback for new memories is unstated, and scope is one benchmark with 100 puzzles.

E.statistics.reason: Three runs with SD plus strict scoring, but headline gains are about one baseline SD or less, no CI or significance test, some SD values 0.00 unexplained, 100-puzzle subset; authors note large sampling variance.

E.cost.reason: Token-efficiency plot says similar to baseline but counts only solver reasoning tokens; abstraction (GPT-4.1) and selection (VLM caption / reasoning exploration) costs are not charged; memory runs increase output tokens.
